transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, hi. I guess... I'm here because of elevators. I mean, I know they aren't really dangerous, but... when I have to get in one, I just get scared. Like I'm gonna get trapped in there, and... I just can't make myself feel normal about it.
Do you experience similar fears or anxieties in situations other than being in elevators?
No... not really. Just elevators. I don't think I get like that with anything else.
Do you avoid using elevators because of this fear?

Yeah, I try not to. Most days I just... take the stairs. At my apartment, or at work on the job sites. If an elevator or a lift is the only way up, I usually just ask to do something else. Or... I guess I'll ride it if someone I trust is right there next to me. But I really try not to.
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes, with symptoms like a racing heart or shortness of breath?
No, I don't think so. I mean, my heart beats a little fast when I have to look at an elevator, but... not like what you're saying. Not out of nowhere.
How long have you been experiencing this fear of elevators?
About 11 months, I guess. It just... started after we lost our house. We had to move into an apartment on one of the upper floors, and... yeah. Just since then.
Is it the elevator itself that scares you, or is it more about the situation of being in a closed or high place?
I don't know. Just... the elevator, I guess. I just don't like them.
Would you feel anxious or scared in other small, enclosed spaces like a closet or a small room?
No, not really. Just... just the elevators.
Would your fear be less if you were in a elevator on the ground floor, not having to go up?
I don't really know. I haven't... I never really tried just standing in one. I just try to stay out of them.
Would you feel scared if you were on a high floor, but not in an elevator?
No... not really. Being up high is fine. It's just... it's just the elevators.
Would you feel scared if you were in a stationary elevator, not moving, with the doors open?
I don't really know. I just... I don't get in them at all, so I couldn't say.
Do you think your fear of elevators is connected to feeling like you're not in control when you're inside one?
I don't know about all that. I haven't really... thought about it like that. I just don't like being in 'em.
Has your fear of elevators significantly changed your daily routine or caused you any problems at work or in your personal life?

I mean... I still get to work, and my GED class. It's not stopping me from doing that. It's just... taking the stairs everywhere, it wears me out. Sometimes it makes me a little late. And on the site... if a job means I gotta take a lift up, I just have to pass on it. Guess it makes me a bit less useful to the crew sometimes. But I manage.
Do you think your fear would decrease if you were in control of the elevator, like if you were the one operating it?
I don't really know. I've never... I've never operated one. I just stay away from them.
Do you think your fear of elevators would decrease if you had a way to escape or get help at any moment while you were inside?
I mean... maybe? I don't really know. I just... I wouldn't want to get in one to find out. I'd rather just stick to the stairs.
Do you think your fear of elevators started because of something specific that happened to you when you moved into the apartment, or is it just the elevator itself that scares you?

I don't think it was... anything specific. Nothing bad happened in it. It's just... it's just the elevator. It started about 11 months ago, when we lost the house and had to move into that upper-floor apartment. That's when I first had to deal with them every day.
Is your fear of elevators because of the elevator itself or because you feel trapped when you're inside?

I guess... it's just being trapped. I know they aren't actually dangerous. But when I have to get in one, I just get this feeling like I'm going to be stuck in there. I can't really... talk myself out of it. It just doesn't feel normal.
Would your fear decrease if you were in a different type of enclosed space that is similar to an elevator, but not actually an elevator?
I... I don't really know. I haven't been in anything else like that to find out. So... I'm not sure.
Would you feel scared or anxious if you were in a small, enclosed space that is not an elevator, like a subway car or a small train compartment?
I haven't really been on a subway or a train lately. So I... I couldn't tell you. I just know the elevator at the apartment is... it's a problem.
Would you feel anxious or scared in a small, enclosed space like a subway car?
Like I just said... I don't really know. I don't ride the subway. So... I couldn't tell you if it would bother me or not. I just know the elevator is the thing I actually have to deal with.
